excerpt: BYJU'S is the Bengaluru edtech company behind The Learning App. Its parent, Think & Learn, has been in insolvency proceedings since 2024.
content:
BYJU'S is an Indian education company best known for its K-12 learning app and exam-preparation courses. Its website today offers free study material and live videos for Classes 1 to 12, NCERT solutions, sample papers and preparation for exams such as IAS, CAT, bank exams and GATE.

KrAsia reported that BYJU'S started in 2011 as an offline tutoring business run by Byju Raveendran, a former engineer who first coached friends for the CAT exam, and that the company was incorporated as Think and Learn. According to the same report, the learning app for school students followed in 2015, about a month after a USD 25 million investment led by Sequoia.

At its peak the company was one of the world's most valuable edtech startups. TechCrunch reported in March 2022 that Raveendran put USD 400 million into an USD 800 million round, alongside Sumeru Ventures, Vitruvian Partners and BlackRock, and that the round valued BYJU'S at about USD 22 billion, citing a person familiar with the matter.

Since 2024 the parent company, Think & Learn Pvt Ltd, has been in corporate insolvency proceedings. LiveLaw reported that on 23 October 2024 the Supreme Court set aside an NCLAT order that had closed the insolvency case on the basis of a roughly Rs 158 crore settlement with the BCCI, which revived the process. Inc42 reported on 23 July 2026 that the NCLT had paused the bidding stage of the process until a hearing on 31 August, while the founders contested a INR 11,433 crore claim by the trustee for US term-loan lenders; the insolvency process itself continued.

BYJU'S does not publish course prices on its website. Anyone considering a paid course should check the company's current status and the refund terms in writing before paying. This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting. We have not tested the product for this page, and nothing here is paid placement.

Its parent, Think & Learn Pvt Ltd, has been in corporate insolvency proceedings since 2024. The Supreme Court revived the process in October 2024, and in July 2026 the NCLT paused the bidding stage while a lender claim is disputed.
TechCrunch reported a valuation of about USD 22 billion in a March 2022 funding round, citing a person familiar with the matter.
No. Its website does not list course fees.
